newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay share index plunges 2.3 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay share index plunges 2.3 pct in late trade.

text.p: Bombay's benchmark stocks index plunged 70.37 points or 2.31 percent to 2972.93 in late trade on Friday, traders said.
They said fund selling in auto stocks TELCO, Mahindra and Bajaj Auto were dragging the 30-share index lower.
Auto analysts said rumours that October auto figures were expected to show a sharp slowdown in sales were untrue.
TELCO slid 26.50 rupees or 7.06 percent to 350, Bajaj Auto fell 20 rupees or 2.18 percent to 896 and Mahindra & Mahindra lost 22.50 rupees or 7.02 percent to 298.
Traders said punters were sellers in these stocks after a couple of foreign funds sold TELCO and Bajaj in early trade.
Rumours that TELCO's October sales show a sharp slowdown from the year-ago were untrue, analysts said.

"TELCO's total sales for October are at 16,822 vehicles, up 26.2 percent from the year-ago and down 5.2 percent from September which is traditionally when sales peak," said an auto analyst at a foreign brokerage firm, quoting unofficial figures.
Official auto figures for October are due early next week.
"Fundamentally, nothing has changed. But sentiment has taken a beating with many investors not expecting the stock to outperform in the next eight to ten months," the analyst said.
He said Bajaj Auto sales were at 120,389 in October, up 16 percent from the year-ago and up 1.8 percent from September.
A sharp 8.96 percent fall in IDBI shares also pulled the index lower, traders said.
IDBI shares dropped 9.25 rupees to 94 after the firm's net profit for the first half to September 30, 1996 fell below market expectations.
